result: Kept. The laughter is seen on every suitor (arms up, each on his own clock) from the first shot; at the seer's standing the hall goes red: red light, the dark red streaks on the walls, the ghosts standing in the porch behind him, and he looks round at them and recoils; his vision is spoken over him and the laughing men; he goes out through the ghosts; the light comes back white for father and son, who look at one another and nod. Loose: the 'darkness' reads as red light more than dark; the meat's blood drops are too small to see in the wides; several frames have a suitor's gold head or a column in the foreground (10.7-15 s); the ending is a mid on the beggar against a bare corner, the feast not in frame; the father-and-son closes 39-46 s are fairly still (0.43-0.79), as the scene's held look is.
